title: Token-Picker: Accelerating Attention in Text Generation with Minimized Memory Transfer via Probability Estimation
problem: Attention mechanism in text generation is memory-bounded with excessive off-chip memory accesses. Existing token pruning methods fail to selectively remove tokens with near-zero attention probabilities on a per-instance basis.
motivation: Minimizing memory bandwidth is critical for efficient inference in large language models where attention becomes the bottleneck.
method: Token-Picker estimates attention probabilities before the softmax function to identify and prune low-probability tokens without fine-tuning. A hardware design supports seamless on-demand off-chip memory access, achieving 12.1x pruning ratio and reducing memory accesses by 2.6x.
key_novelty: Pre-softmax probability estimation enables instance-specific token pruning that removes near-zero probability tokens without model retraining.
contributions: Pre-softmax probability estimation for selective token pruning without fine-tuning
Hardware design supporting on-demand off-chip memory access
2.3x average speedup with 2.4x energy efficiency improvement
limitations: Limitations and broader impact not discussed in abstract.
